reference_book.title: The Book of the Unnamed Midwife (The Road to Nowhere, #1)
reference_book.review_text:
It took me a while to get into this book - these old eyes didn't deal well with the change of font. But thank goodness for Kindles and the ability to change the size of the fonts! This is an excellent apocalyptic/PA book about a virus that kills most of the people in the world - and even more women than men, and ALL the babies at birth. How can we have hope and keep trudging on in a changed world without the hope of a future with children? 
 The "unnamed" person is a midwife on the coast of California when the disease hits. She struggles with losing both babies and mothers. Then, she too gets sick with the mysterious fever. But...she wakes up eventually and sets off to find a place to make a life. The trek is hard and cruel, and she meets a few real crazies along the way. 
 I loved this book!

book_a.title: Article 5 (Article 5, #1)
book_a.user_review: I liked this book okay - enough that I will continue on with the series. BUT - I had a hard time with about the first 1/3 - it was just TOO YA. There are flashbacks to her first kiss, first love...and it goes on a bit too much for this old broad. After that the mushy flashbacks end, she seems to grow up a bit, and the action gets...more active?

sample_reviews.review_text:
I thought that this was really great! I have been wanting to read this for a while, and then my sister finally got it for Easter and of course she instantly hid it away from me, but I have at last gotten my hands on it. I love the premise of the book. And I know that sometimes the post apocalyptic world is a bit overdone and everyone's just dying and there's no hope, but I never get tired of it. I love the end of the world books. And I love Chase and Ember's relationship. Their relationship is so complex and there is so much going on between them, but at the same time, the reader is never confused. They can relate because everyone has had someone in their life who they were close with and then they dramatically changed and you're just left so confused about what happened. That's how Ember feels, and probably Chase too. And they just don't know how to get back to where they were after so much has happened. I thought it was so good, and I am getting the next one, Breaking Point as soon as I can. 
 If you liked Legend, I would recommend this book.

the fuck...the girl is so stupid plus annoying plus idk whatever happened to those intelligent, daring, irresistibly admirable old fashioned heroines...i want to read a book about them, instead of all these craps :( 
 unbearable road trip theme..seriously, dystopian society and road trip just doesn't go along, unless ofcourse there are zombies lol and once again..what the fuck is wrong with this girl? first she tries to take on the arresting officers, then she tries to plan an escape, she has no regards for anyone else, she thinks she is going to break out save her mother bla bla i mean she acts like she has a superpower or something..one girl against the world...lol, seriously, saving the world? she is more likely to slip off a banana peel and die...seeing how much brain and common sense this girl poses.

I think I may have read too many Dystopian books in a row. I found Ember to be a very realistic teen girl throw into a horrible world and stumbling her way along. She doesn't wallow in self pity but tries to find a way to fight and get out and survive. 
 But, even though she was a great main character, I just didn't connect to her. I think that had a lot to do with the fact that I just couldn't buy this dystopian world. If we destroy all and go to rebuild, I just can't imagine this is how it will be. And since I had tough time with the world, I had a tough time with the book 
 But, I did like Ember and Chase. I liked the underground world they ended up trudging through, their shot at trying to survive in cold weather with little food and not enough sleeping bags and the strange love/hate/hurt/struggle thing they had going on. Chase and Ember (and some of the supporting characters) are reason alone to read this book.

I found this book to be rather problematic; while the concept intrigued me in its comparison to Nazi Germany, the forced romantic tension between the main character and her ex/love interest was so ridiculous that I was rolling my eyes more often than feeling any type of feeling towards the main characters. I really just wanted to yell at Ember to tell her to stop whining and say what she was thinking rather than just whining about her issues. I will not read any sequels to this books since the character development was so lacking that I really do not care what happens to the characters.

I didn't finish this book and know that I won't. I tried, I really did. The heroine was annoying and the book was just so easy to put down and not pick up again. After I checked GoodReads, I realised that it wasn't going to improve so I decided not to waste my time. To say it wasn't a page turner is an understatement.

I enjoyed this book immensely! It's a great dystopian novel and the story sucked me in and wouldn't let me go! It's got the angsty feeling, the harsh environment, the rush to save someone, the need to save each other...I really liked it!

Why???? This was the question I asked the entire book. And not in a good way. Sigh.

This was an okay book...I was looking for a good dystopian adventure and, although it started out well, went downhill from there. I realize the protagonist was a teenager, but her back-and-forth deliberations and decisions seemed more those of a 14-year old, not an almost-18 year old. And the way that Chase and Ember didn't talk to each other - with the history they had - was incredibility unbelievable to me. Do I want to know what happens in book two? Sort of....

I've had this on my list for a while, but haven't read it yet because of the mixed reviews. Now getting into it, I see why (and I was right to wait). 
 Article 5 is about a girl named Ember who gets arrested early on in the book because of Article 5, one of the mandates now in the United States. Don't ask me why a War (you always know if it's in capital letters, it's IMPORTANT-- no, not being sarcastic AT ALL) would create this mandate, or why people would think it was the way to stop wars, but whatever. So she loves this boy, Chase, who of course is a soldier that helps enforce these rules. 
 I admit that I could only get through 45% of this book before giving up. And there was at least 10% that I was skimming, hoping to make it to the end, just so I could see if there were any redeeming twists. But I was so fed up with the lack of world building, the vagueness of the whole situation, and the really annoying and unlikeable protagonist, Ember. I was hoping the whining and bad attitude would get better, but she basically just blames everyone else for her problems. I know life is bad, but eventually, you have to move on and try to get through the awfulness that is going on. Otherwise, you might as well just give up. In real life, this chick wouldn't have made it past the first few chapters. After scratching that guard, she would have been killed. Her relationship with her mother is completely unhealthy, and focusing on that as the big emotional connection in the book felt very false. Not to mention Chase-- if I were him, I would have dumped her on the side of the road a long time ago. 
 Overall, a huge disappointment, and I couldn't even finish it.

book_b.title: Where She Went (If I Stay, #2)
book_b.user_review: I loved If I Stay, and this 2nd book is a very satisfying follow up. Just what happened in the 3 years between when Mia left for Julliard, and when Adam attended her concert in NYC? This book tells the story, from Adam's point of view. It alternates between present day and the past, to fill us in on what they have been doing the past 3 years. It made me cry at points, it also made me smile. It left me hopeful. I highly recommend that anyone who read the 1st book read this follow up.

sample_reviews.review_text: I absolutely loved IF I STAY, so when I heard there would be a sequel from Adam's POV I was thrilled! Gayle Forman does NOT disappoint. Just read it.

I think that Adam Wilde might be the most unlikeable character I've read in a very, very long while. 
 I did not read this book for his diatribey, paranoid, privileged, whiney, misogynistic male tears. I read this book for Mia. Unfortunately, Mia is only present in half of the book, and even for that half we have to slog through Adams bullshit hangups as narration about their past. I seriously hate Adam Wilde. 
 Although, I didn't hate the ending. It seemed right because it was a very young adult literature way to tie up the story. I would have, however, LOVED if the ending were different. I would have loved to see more of Mia's process and agency and seen her make a different decision and force Wahdum to deal with it. But it still gave me a warm feeling to see things tied up the way they did.
It was a good book, liked the first one better though :)

Wow! Aunque de una manera u otra sabia como terminaria la historia no me parecio un cliche. Adam logro enamorarme en la forma que cuenta su historia. De lo que a sentido y pasado en esos tres anos que pasaron separados, lo que sufrio y lo que no lograba comprender
I love it when authors can write the same story in different perspectives and still suck me in. Such a lovely story :) quick read

People always say that the first book/movie isn't better than the first, but that is absolutely not true about this particular mini series. Reading it from Adam's view changed my whole prospective and was even more heart wrenching than the first. I am so in love with Adam and Mia, more so than I was in the first book. You truly feel that you are right beside them through it all and the imagery is perfect.
Not bad, but not as good as the first,
Love the idea of the book and would have given it more stars if the swearing wasn't so offensive. It just isn't necessary.

Wow, I am speechless. What an amazingly beautiful book! Adam is a hot, hot mess and such a compelling and complex character. Gayle Forman has outdone herself, and I'm sure I'll be thinking about these characters for a long time.
